objective: Repair two measured defects in the instrument that scores this lab's own cost forecasting, one of which marks a perfectly correct forecast as infinitely wrong and the other of which evaluates a three-in-a-row-over-time rule over an alphabetical list, and require every streak criterion in this lab to declare the key it orders on
rationale: Both defects were reproduced on 2026-08-14 by running the instrument and then re-deriving its arithmetic independently. DEFECT ONE, a gate failing false. The relative error is formed by dividing by the measured cost, with a guard that substitutes infinity when the measured cost is zero. Two closed records were forecast at zero core minutes and measured at zero core minutes. A forecast that was exactly right is printed as a miss at infinite percent. This is the lab's own second defect class arriving in the instrument that grades the lab. Its effect on the published headline is measured, not asserted: the instrument reports a hit rate of 3 of 11; the two degenerate records are neither hits nor misses and belong in a third class, which leaves 3 of 9 as the real forecasting rate and shows the published figure to be wrong in BOTH directions at once depending on how the degenerate pair is handled. DEFECT TWO, a frame nobody stated. A standing rule requires three consecutive forecasts within tolerance before a capability may be claimed. The implementation takes the last three entries of a list built by iterating the inbox in sorted filename order. Measured: the three the rule currently inspects are the three records whose names happen to sort last. Re-sorted on the records' own completion and execution timestamps, the last three are an entirely different set. The rule is written about time and evaluated about the alphabet, so it has never once tested the thing it says it tests. THE NULL, AND IT IS NOT FITTED: the current implementation's own output, taken before any edit, which is on the record. THE IDENTITY TEST, owner rule W dash 2, and it is the reason this item does not simply reclassify the degenerate pair as hits. Could the scored quantity be derived by construction from its own inputs? For the ordinary records, no: the forecast is written before the work and the measurement after, and they share no computation. For a record forecast at zero and measured at zero, YES, trivially: the pair carries no information about anybody's forecasting ability, because a task with no solver in it was always going to cost no core minutes. Counting those as hits would inflate the rate from 3 of 11 to 5 of 11 on two records that tested nothing. So the repair is NOT to call them hits and NOT to call them misses, but to report them as a named third class of degenerate pairs, excluded from the rate and printed with their count. And note what the corrected instrument does NOT do, which is the check that the fix is not self-serving: under both repairs together the standing three-in-a-row rule remains unsatisfied, because the corrected time-ordered triple reads as a hit, a miss and a hit. A repair that had flipped the gate green would have been the suspicious outcome.
gate: ZERO COMPUTE. Three deliverables, each with its own falsifier. ONE: the degenerate class. A pair whose forecast and measurement are both zero is reported in a named third class with its count and is excluded from the rate; the printed rate then carries its denominator explicitly. Falsifier: if excluding them changes the rate by less than the instrument's own reporting precision, the change is cosmetic and should be recorded as such rather than claimed as a repair. TWO: the ordering key. The streak rule sorts on a stated timestamp field with a stated fallback chain, prints the key it used and prints the identifiers of the records the streak actually inspected, so the frame is on the face of the output. Falsifier: if the time-ordered and filename-ordered triples turn out to be the same set, the defect is latent rather than active, and the record must say so. MEASURED IN ADVANCE: they are not the same set. THREE, and this is the part worth more than the two fixes: a sweep for every other place in this lab where a criterion counts consecutive events, and a requirement that each states its ordering key. The sweep must plant its own positive control inside an ignored path, because this shell's search honours ignore files and sees roughly a quarter of the tree, and a sweep for streak criteria that silently misses them is the first defect class wearing the costume of a repair for the second.
cost_basis: ZERO solver compute. Scored in agent tool calls: forecast 40, inside this lab's measured build-and-verify band of 33 to 72 because the item edits a script, adds tests and runs a corpus sweep with a planted control. Actual counted from the executing agent's transcript. The diagnosis half is already spent and is reported here rather than re-billed: both defects were reproduced during the drafting of this proposal at 2 tool calls.
expected_knowledge_gain: THE DISCRIMINATING OUTCOME. The lab's published statement about its own forecasting changes numerically and in frame: the rate acquires a stated denominator that excludes pairs which tested nothing, and the standing capability rule starts inspecting records ordered by when the work happened. The third deliverable is where belief could move furthest: if the sweep finds other consecutive-event criteria with unstated ordering keys, then a whole family of this lab's gates has the same unexamined frame and the finding generalises past one script; if it finds none, the defect is isolated and that is worth knowing too, because it bounds the class. Belief would be unmoved only if the sweep were allowed to return an unverified zero, which the planted control forbids.
hard_criterion_note: Starts no flow case. Arithmetic and source edits over records already on disk.

launch_prompt: Calibration instrument repair. ZERO COMPUTE. Step 1: run the scorecard unchanged and commit its output as the before state; do not edit first. Step 2: implement the degenerate third class and the stated ordering key, each with a test that fails on the current code. Clear any compiled bytecode caches between mutation cells -- this lab has a measured case of a mutation matrix reading exactly inverted through a stale cache, and setting the do-not-write-bytecode environment variable does NOT fix it. Step 3: re-run and print the before and after side by side, and state explicitly whether the standing three-in-a-row rule changed verdict; if it flipped to satisfied, STOP and report that as a suspicious result rather than a success. Step 4: the sweep for other consecutive-event criteria, with a planted positive control inside an ignored path, and state the frame of the count. Record your own tool call count.
